relevance_note: Case report of one boy with a heterozygous TNFAIP3 nonsense variant: "we present a patient with a novel mutation in the TNFAIP3 gene".
method_note: Single-patient case report read in full; the JSON was assembled with a short Python script from values I transcribed by reading, and every span was checked verbatim against the paper by script. In scope: the index patient (label 'patient', rule 5); both parents as tested-negative relatives ('father of patient', 'mother of patient'; segregation analysis negative; both have migraine, mother had gestational diabetes); and, under the v3 rule for summarised earlier reports, the two children of reference (8) ('a 3-year-old and a 6-month-old child with HA20'), labelled 'ref (8) patient' and 'ref (8) patient 2' in order of mention. The text gives no variant for the ref (8) children and does not tie a TNFAIP3 variant to them individually (only 'with HA20'), so they have no variant rows; the sentence 'the concentration of serum IgG was elevated as it was also in our patient' does not say which ref (8) child(ren), so it was not recorded for either. Group-level literature (the first cohort of 16 patients, ref 4; Yu et al. 61 patients, ref 6; Schwartz et al., ref 9) gives counts only and produced no rows. Contradiction/inconsistency: the Case presentation says 'Fevers started at 7 weeks of age' and abdominal pain from 2.5 years, whereas the Discussion says abdominal pains, diarrhea and fever attacks were present 'since early infancy, from the age of 2 years old'; onset recorded from the Case presentation. GI: histology showed 'non-specific mild inflammatory changes' (Discussion: 'non-specific chronic inflammation on gut biopsy') while ultrasound and MR enterography showed no signs of inflammation; treated as different modalities, not a contradiction, so the checklist GI item is observed. Checklist choices: 'no arthritis' and 'no rash' do not exclude the composite arthritis-or-arthralgia and skin-lesion items (left not reported; muscle pains = myalgia, not arthralgia); a negative ANA and normal celiac serology do not exclude the composite autoantibodies (ANA/other) item (left not reported); 'pronounced lymphatic hypertrophy in the terminal ileum' was not mapped to lymphoproliferation; decreased CD4+/CD8+ T cells were not mapped to autoimmune cytopenia; growth failure excluded from 'His growth and development were within normal limits' although intrauterine growth retardation is recorded separately as a prenatal feature. Diagnostic exclusions of other diseases (cystic fibrosis testing negative, normal NBT for chronic granulomatous disease, normal karyotype, 'Infections were excluded' in the GI work-up) were not recorded as phenotypic features. Table 1/2 numeric values were not interpreted beyond what the text states; Table 2 data rows look duplicated by the merged-cell conversion, which affects no extracted value. Age at diagnosis is not stated (genetic result in November 2018; age not given). Vital status 'alive' is from the follow-up description.
